Top candidates from the leaf set: **Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus** (bronzing, necrotic spots, downward cupping), **Bacterial_Speck_Of_Tomato** (small black spots with halos), **Septoria_Leaf_Blotch** (small dark spots).

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with TSWV.
Good match — TSWV shows bronzing, scattered dark necrotic spots. Now checking Bacterial Speck.
Bacterial Speck shows yellow halos and green leaves — less matching. Now checking Septoria.
Septoria doesn't match — different color pattern. Now checking TSWV second reference for more detail.
TSWV Bugwood_181 shows ring patterns — different from the test. Now checking Bacterial Canker which could explain the dark stem/petiole cluster.
Bacterial Canker shows marginal scorching — different pattern. Let me check Verticillium Wilt and Late Blight.
Verticillium shows V-shaped yellowing — doesn't match. Now checking Late Blight leaf reference.
Late Blight microscope image — not useful. Need one more class. Checking Early Blight.

Early Blight shows large concentric-ring lesions — clearly doesn't match.

**Summary of comparisons:**
- **TSWV Bugwood_10**: Best match — bronzing, scattered small dark necrotic spots, similar grayish tint, small dark lesions scattered across leaves
- Bacterial Speck: Yellow halos, greener leaves — less matching
- Septoria: Yellow discoloration — no match
- TSWV Bugwood_181: Ring patterns — different presentation
- Bacterial Canker: Marginal scorching — no match
- Verticillium Wilt: V-shaped yellowing, wilting — no match
- Late Blight Bugwood_10: Microscopic spores — not usable
- Early Blight: Large concentric ring lesions — no match

The test image's grayish-bronzed leaves with scattered small dark necrotic spots and a dark necrotic cluster at the apical/petiole junction matches TSWV most closely. TSWV causes bronzing on upper leaf surfaces, distinct necrotic spots, and tip dieback/necrosis — all visible in the test image.
